findings.title: Invalid Ruby syntax `<%- end if %>` in ERB template causes SyntaxError
findings.body: Line 6 closes the `if` block with `<%- end if %>`, which is not valid Ruby syntax (Ruby uses `end`, not `end if`). When `EmbedController#best` renders `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`, ERB compilation will fail with a `SyntaxError` because `if` has no condition following `end`.

findings.title: `raw_html` cook method bypasses HTML sanitization and post filters, enabling stored XSS
findings.body: When `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly without passing it through `Sanitize` or `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)`. Posts imported via `Jobs::PollFeed` (`app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:36`) pass raw RSS `<content>` directly into `TopicEmbed.import` with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`. Any `<script>` tags, inline event handlers (`onload`, `onerror`), or `javascript:` URLs in the RSS feed (or if a regular user edits a `raw_html` post) will be stored verbatim in `cooked` and rendered unescaped to all users viewing the topic.

findings.title: `Kernel#open` called with external URL allows command/file read injection and SSRF
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read` (via `open-uri`) on `url`. While `TopicRetriever` checks that `URI(embed_url).host == SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, `URI('http://allowed-host/|malicious_command').host` or similar tricks, or callers like `Disqus#import` (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor:148`) that pass URLs from an XML export without any scheme/host validation, can pass strings starting with `|` or local file paths to `Kernel#open`, leading to arbitrary command execution or local file disclosure. Even with HTTP URLs, `open-uri` follows redirects to `file://` or internal network hosts (SSRF) if `embeddable_host` redirects. Use `URI.parse(url).open` (or `Net::HTTP` / `RestClient`) after verifying the scheme is `http` or `https`.

findings.title: `TopicEmbed.import` mutates the caller's `contents` string in place, breaking frozen strings
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` uses `contents << ...` to append the imported-from footer, which mutates the `contents` argument in place. If a caller passes a frozen string or reuses the string across calls, this will raise `RuntimeError: can't modify frozen String` or append duplicate footers. Use `contents = "#{contents}\n<hr>..."` or `contents = contents.dup << ...` instead.

findings.title: `PollFeed#poll_feed` crashes with `NoMethodError` when RSS items use `<description>` instead of `<content>` or on Ruby < 2.1
findings.body: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`, `i.content.scrub` assumes two things that frequently do not hold: (1) standard RSS 2.0 feeds populate `i.description` rather than `i.content`, so `i.content` is `nil` and calling `.scrub` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'scrub' for nil:NilClass`; (2) `String#scrub` was only introduced in Ruby 2.1, whereas this repo supports Ruby 1.9/2.0 (see `Gemfile` line 213). Fallback to `i.description` when `i.content` is blank and guard against `nil`.

findings.title: Adding `force: true` to an existing migration will drop `top_topics` data if re-run
findings.body: `20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` is an existing migration unrelated to topic embeds, and changing `create_table :top_topics` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` causes the table to be dropped and recreated if the migration is run against a database that already has `top_topics`. This looks like an accidental leftover from local migration testing.
